findings.claim: Headline CPI accelerated to 3.71% y/y as energy rebounded, while monthly core CPI and core PCE also firmed even as core CPI's y/y rate eased.
Labor signals softened at the margin, with unemployment rising and payroll growth slowing, while initial claims edged down.
Industrial production growth improved to 1.42% y/y, a firmer activity signal against the softer labor readings.

A one-day Treasury rally has not erased month-long duration pressure: 10-year yields remain higher, while long-duration Treasuries and credit ETFs are lower and the dollar has strengthened against the euro.
Technology continues to lead, while financials, industrials and consumer discretionary remain down over the month, so equity strength has not broadly spread to cyclicals.
Fed minutes showed most officials considered another hike likely by year-end, after September’s increase took the policy rate to about 3.9%.

findings.claim: The 30-year Treasury yield briefly reached a 24-year high of 5.7041% as long-end Treasuries sold off.
French fiscal stress weighed on the euro, which fell 0.65%, while the dollar index strengthened.

note.headline: Long-end Treasury yields reached fresh highs as Fed minutes pointed to another hike and markets raised the odds of still-higher yields.
takeaways: The 30-year Treasury yield briefly reached 5.7041%, while prediction-market odds shifted toward a higher long-end yield.
Fed officials saw another hike as likely by year-end, even as October hold odds rose.
Monthly core inflation firmed as labor softened, and technology’s equity leadership remained narrow.

items.title: Long-end yield pressure persists
items.body: The 30-year Treasury yield briefly reached 5.7041%, while the 10-year yield remained +49.00bp over the month despite a -4.00bp day. Polymarket odds of the 30-year yield reaching 5.80% before 2027 rose +14.8pp to 68.7%.

items.title: Monthly inflation firms
items.body: Headline CPI accelerated to 3.71% y/y as energy rebounded. Core CPI rose 0.29% m/m and core PCE rose 0.25% m/m, even as core CPI eased to 2.76% y/y.

items.title: Later hike, October hold
items.body: Fed minutes showed most officials considered another hike likely by year-end. Polymarket odds of no change at the October meeting rose +18.0pp over the week to 83.5%.

items.title: Labor softens, production improves
items.body: Unemployment rose to 4.20% and payroll growth slowed to 0.31% y/y, while initial claims edged down. Industrial production growth improved to 1.42% y/y, offering a firmer activity signal.

items.title: Technology leadership stays narrow
items.body: Technology gained +7.32% over the month, while financials fell -5.86%, industrials -3.51% and consumer discretionary -2.09%. Equity strength has not spread broadly to cyclicals.

themes_touched.title: Duration pressure and stronger-dollar stress
themes_touched.text: Long-end Treasury yields reached fresh highs despite a one-day retreat in yields, and prediction-market odds shifted further toward higher long-end yields. The dollar also strengthened against the euro over the month.

themes_touched.title: Narrow technology leadership versus cyclical weakness
themes_touched.text: Technology continued to lead over the month while financials, industrials and consumer discretionary declined, leaving equity strength concentrated rather than broadly cyclical.

new_themes.title: Firmer inflation amid softer labor
new_themes.text: Monthly core inflation firmed while unemployment rose and payroll growth slowed. Improving industrial production complicates the activity picture.
